questions.question: What type of hydraulic filter is used on aircraft and how does a hydraulic filter operate?
questions.idealAnswer: Most hydraulic filters are in-line micronic type. Filter elements may be micronic, porous metal, or magnetic type. Most micronic filters are made of paper. Fluid enters the filter through a port in the filter head and must pass through the filter element to exit. Should the element be clogged a bypass in the filter head will allow unfiltered fluid to flow to the hydraulic system. Differential pressure indicators to alert the technician or crew that the filter is being bypassed.

questions.question: Describe some maintenance procedures used for hydraulic filters.
questions.idealAnswer: Hydraulic filters are cleaned or replaced periodically in accordance with the maintenance manufacture's manual instructions. Replaceable filter elements must be inspected to make sure they are not damaged. Paper filter elements must be discarded. Magnetic type and porous metal filters are cleaned inspected and reinstalled. When replacing filter elements it is crucial to make sure the hydraulic systems pressure is depleted. Personal protective equipment must be observed. Also after filter is replaced a technician must pressurize the hydraulic system and check for leaks.

questions.question: Describe the purpose of relief valves and pressure regulators in a hydraulic system.
questions.idealAnswer: A relief valve is used to limit the pressure being exerted on a confined liquid. In the hydraulic system, this protects components from failure do to excessive pressure. When pressure reaches a pre-determined pressure the relief valve opens to protect the system. Pressure relief valves can also be installed to relieve pressure due to thermal expansion. Pressure regulators are used to manage the output pressure of the pump, to maintain system operating pressure within a predetermined range. Another purpose for a pressure regulator is to permit the pump to turn without resistance, this is known as unloading the pump.

questions.question: What are some Hydraulic system maintenance precautions used to prevent contamination?
questions.idealAnswer: Only the correct, specified fluid must be used to service an aircraft hydraulic system. Keep all tools and work area clean. Use a proper container for capturing hydraulic fluid. Clean the fittings and area around them. Cap and plug all lines immediately after disconnecting. Before assembly, wash all parts in approved solvent. lubricate parts and seals before assembly. Replace all seals and gaskets with new. Only use seals and gaskets with the proper part number. Connect and torque all lines. Make sure hydraulic tools and equipment are clean and in good operating condition.

questions.question: What are some common types and characteristics of hydraulic fluids, where are they used and how can they be identified?
questions.idealAnswer: There are three types of hydraulic fluids: Mineral- based, Polyalaphaolefins, Phosphate esters. Mineral- based fluid is processed from from petroleum. It is dyed red and and has an odor similar to penetrating oil. The most common is MIL-H-5606. Mostly used in small aircraft where fire hazard is low. Polyalaphaolefins, oil is more fire resistant type of hydraulic oil, sometimes used in aircraft that normally use MIL-H- 5606. It is compatible with the same seals used for mineral based hydraulic systems. Phosphate ester-based (Skydrol) hydraulic fluid is used mostly in commercial transport category aircraft. It is dyed purple and fire resistant but not fire proof. Due to the difference in composition Phosphate ester-based and 5606 will not mix, and the seals used are also incompatible with the other. Do not try to mix hydraulic fluids, each hydraulic fluid is dyed a different color as to easily identify which hydraulic fluid it is. Always check the maintenance manual for the correct fluid to be used.

questions.question: What are some health handling factors when using Phosphate ester- based hydraulic fluid?
questions.idealAnswer: Skydrol on the skin can cause burning and an itching sensation. Prolong exposure can cause dry skin and could cause dermatitis or a secondary infection from bacteria. Always wear proper gloves and eye protection when handling Phosphate ester based (Skydrol) hydraulic fluid. When vapor exposure is possible, a respirator should be worn. Avoid ingesting any type of hydraulic fluid, any significant amount of ingested hydraulic fluid should be followed up by medical supervised testing and surveillance.

questions.question: What does an unloading valve do in a hydraulic system?
questions.idealAnswer: An unloading valve or, (pressure regulator) controls system pressure by shifting pump outlet fluid from the pressurized system back into reservoir when system pressure is high enough (‘kick out’ pressure). The fluid circulates in the system with little load on the pump until system pressure drops to a specified ‘kick in’ pressure, at which point the pump forces fluid back into the pressurized system.
